1.mascotDialogue: Once the expression's a tree, evaluating it is simple — solve both children, then apply the operator at the parent. No precedence table needed at evaluation time — the shape already knows the order, güey.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8's the base case — a leaf just returns its digit. Lines 9 and 10 recurse into both children before line 11 combines 'em. Bottom of the tree evaluates first, siempre.

3.mascotDialogue: Because plus sits under times, it's forced to resolve first — that's precedence, shown as depth in the tree instead of some rule you gotta memorize.

4.mascotDialogue: This bug hides good precisely because multiplication doesn't care about order. Swap the operator to subtraction in your head, and this exact same shape starts lying to you.
